Agents at Scale: AI Deployment Crosses From Pilot to Production

By Will Zheng · April 6, 2026 · From Issue #5

Google Cloud / Deloitte / Goldman Sachs Industry

Multiple major reports converged this week confirming that AI agent deployment has crossed a threshold: 86% of organizations plan to increase AI budgets in 2026, and autonomous agent use is now in active production — not just pilots — across telecom (48% agentic deployment), retail and CPG (47%), and financial services. Deloitte's State of AI in Enterprise found that only 22% of companies have AI actively running in operations, which makes the adoption gap concrete: most organizations are budgeting for AI while remaining in a pre-production state. Goldman Sachs added a productivity dimension — employees with enterprise AI access save 40–60 minutes per day, and 75% report completing tasks they previously could not do at all — but noted that 80% of U.S. companies are not yet actively deploying, and executives privately project AI-attributed workforce changes at nine times the rate of public disclosures. The data governance, infrastructure, and organizational change barriers cited as primary blockers all point in the same direction: technology readiness is far ahead of process readiness, and the bottleneck is structural, not technical.
